verdicts.title: A General Method for Constructing Ramanujan Formulas for $1/π^ν$
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: In this article we give the theoretical background for generating Ramanujan type $1/π^{2ν}$ formulas. As applications of our method we give a general construction of $1/π^4$ series and examples of $1/π^6$ series. We also study the elliptic alpha function whose values are useful for such evaluations.
verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract discusses Ramanujan formulas for $1/π^ν$, which does not interact with the specific claim about cumulative entropy and balanced separator size in the conjecture.

verdicts.title: A family of Ramanujan-Orr formulas for $1/π$
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: We use a variant of Wan's method to prove two Ramanujan-Orr type formulas for $1/π$. This variant needs to know in advance the formulas for $1/π$ that we want to prove, but avoids the need of solving a system of equations.
verdicts.judge_reasoning: The cited paper discusses Ramanujan-Orr type formulas for $1/π$, which is unrelated to the conjecture regarding Φ(π) and the cumulative-entropy analogue of space lower bounds in resolution proof complexity. The vocabulary does not intersect, and there is no mention of Φ(π), c·|S|², or balanced separator size.

verdicts.title: Proofs as Execution Trees for the π-Calculus
verdicts.abstract_excerpt:
In this paper, we establish the foundations of a novel logical framework for the π-calculus, based on the deduction-as-computation paradigm. Following the standard proof-theoretic interpretation of logic programming, we represent processes as formulas, and we interpret proofs as computations.
